pages.title: Rooted in this place.
pages.label: About the museum
pages.intro: The museum shares the history of South Central Oklahoma through artifacts collected from around the area, from an early electric car to one of the earliest examples of a steam-pumper fire engine.

sections.title: Our largest artifact is the building itself
sections.text: Built in 1935–1936 by the Works Progress Administration, this limestone armory originally served the local National Guard. The building also served as a roller skating rink. Today, its walls hold the stories of our region.

sections.title: Our mission
sections.text: To collect, preserve and interpret the social, cultural and economic history of South Central Oklahoma with a special emphasis on Ardmore and Carter County.

sections.title: Many stories under one roof
sections.text: Major exhibits are housed in three main wings. The north wing’s Transportation and Industry Gallery explores railroads, cotton and oil, with early carriages, saddles, soapbox derby cars and a model of oil-field equipment. The south wing includes From the Ashes, the Fonville Gallery, the Genealogical Library and items found in early homes of the area. Ardmore’s first steam-powered fire engine is among its highlights.

sections.title: Tools of Our Land
sections.text: Completed in May 2017, two 5,000-square-foot buildings explore the farming and ranching history of the area.

sections.title: Honoring those who served
sections.text: The Military Memorial Museum preserves military history from the American Revolution to the Gulf Wars and honors our nation’s veterans. Its displays include everyday items used by soldiers, models and uniforms representing all eight uniformed services.

pages.title: Honoring those who served.
pages.label: Military Memorial Museum
pages.intro: Preserving military history and honoring the people of all service branches who have served this country in war and peace.

sections.title: History
sections.text: The Military Memorial Museum is housed in the west wing of the building that once served as a National Guard Armory for Oklahoma’s historic, battle-proven 45th Division. Built by the Works Progress Administration in 1935–1936, the building itself is a monument to that period in Oklahoma’s and the nation’s history. The men and women who serve as guides, or “Charge of Quarters,” are volunteers.

sections.title: Exhibits
sections.text: Displays in the museum represent all eras: the Civil War, the Spanish-American War, the Indian Wars, World War I, World War II, the Korean Conflict, Vietnam, the Gulf War and the Iraqi Freedom War. The displays include artifacts, documents, photographs, uniforms, weapons, knives, models, medals and a great deal of personal memorabilia from veterans all over the United States.

sections.title: Mission
sections.text: Our mission from the beginning has been to preserve and display military history, and to honor those persons of all service branches who have served this country in war and peace.

sections.title: Funding
sections.text: Although the Military Memorial Museum is located in the Greater Southwest Historical Museum, it is self-supporting and does not share in the gifts or donations made to the larger museum. Memberships and Hall of Honor donations are important sources of support.

sections.title: Hall of Honor
sections.text: A donation of $50 purchases an engraved plate showing the donor’s name and the name of the recipient being honored. Memorials may be made “In Memory Of” a veteran family member or veteran friend from any state or branch of service. The entrance and main corridor of the Military Memorial Museum are recognized as the Hall of Honor.
links: Ask about membership or a memorial

sections.title: Ardmore Army Air Field history
sections.text: Explore the history of Ardmore Army Air Field (1942–1946) and Ardmore Air Force Base (1953–1959). This memorial website is dedicated to the men and women who served with distinction at Ardmore Army Air Field, a training base for the U.S. Army Air Forces.

pages.title: Gather somewhere memorable.
pages.label: Rent the museum
pages.intro: The museum and its grounds may be available for non-commercial, private functions in a setting surrounded by the history of South Central Oklahoma.

sections.title: Noble Hall
sections.text: A setting for receptions, business meetings, holiday parties and special events. Noble Hall is available outside the museum’s operating hours.

sections.title: The Education Room
sections.text: Located in the north wing, the Education Room suits small meetings, birthday parties, wedding and baby showers, and workshops. It is available during operating hours. A $50 reservation deposit is required. Half-day rental time slots are 10 a.m.–1:30 p.m. or 1:30–5 p.m. Call to reserve a time.

sections.title: Tools of Our Land

pages.title: Be part of the story.
pages.label: Membership
pages.intro: Membership helps keep local history alive through exhibits, education and community programs.

sections.title: Stay connected
sections.text: All membership levels receive quarterly newsletters and invitations to special events. Some levels include additional rental benefits. Contact the museum to join.

sections.title: Membership levels
items: Couple — $35: standard benefits for two people
Family — $50: standard benefits for all family members, plus a 5% rental discount
Business — $100 for a business. Includes standard benefits and a 10% discount on museum rentals for the business.
Sustaining — $100 for an individual. Includes individual benefits and a 10% discount on museum rentals.
Patron — $250: Sustaining benefits, plus one Education Room rental fee waiver
Benefactor — $500: Patron benefits, plus one Noble Hall rental fee waiver

sections.title: Join or renew
sections.text: Memberships renew every January. Ask for the current application, then mail the completed form and a check payable to GSHM to {name}, {address}.

sections.title: Santa’s House on the Prairie
sections.text: You can give to the Museum General Fund or sponsor a Holiday Forest tree. Tree sponsorship helps support Santa’s House on the Prairie. Your name is displayed on a tree in the Holiday Forest, where children listen to stories and watch the Daube Puppets. You may decorate your tree or have museum staff decorate it for an additional fee. Staff will do their best to use your chosen colors or theme. Contact the curator for current sponsorship prices and display dates.

sections.title: Considering an artifact donation?
sections.text: Please speak with the curator before mailing or bringing an item. Unsolicited donations cannot be accepted. Contact Cassandra to discuss the object and request current donation requirements and forms.

sections.title: Learning throughout the museum
sections.text: The museum teaches the history and culture of the area through three-dimensional artifacts, archives and photographs. Educational opportunities are available for groups of all ages. Programs may take place inside the museum, at the 700 Ranch House or in Neustadt Park. Contact us to discuss a setting and program for your group.

pages.title: A little holiday wonder.
pages.label: Santa’s House on the Prairie
pages.intro: Santa’s House on the Prairie is an event designed for schoolchildren ages three to seven years old. Participating children enjoy decorating ornaments, exploring our Holiday Forest, and listening to stories read by Mr. and Mrs. Claus.

sections.title: A memorable morning
sections.text: Begin in the Holiday Forest, hear a story from Santa and visit the craft stations with your group.

sections.title: Plan your group’s visit
sections.text: Santa’s House runs during the first two full weeks of December. Admission is $2 per child. Call the museum to reserve a time for your group.

sections.title: Help make the magic
sections.text: Volunteers help keep the program running throughout its two-week season. Roles include movie attendant, playing Mr. or Mrs. Claus, group attendant and crafting assistant. Contact Cassandra, our curator, by email or call the museum to volunteer.

sections.title: Sponsor a Holiday Forest tree
sections.text: Sponsor a small or large tree in the Holiday Forest to help support Santa’s House. Your name will appear on the tree. Decorate it yourself or have museum staff decorate it for an additional fee. Ask Cassandra about display dates, colors and sponsorship prices.
